subject: Materials Science
title: What Makes Nano Different?
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: What Makes Nano Different?.

hook.text: Gold is yellow. Shrink it to 20 nanometers and it turns red. At the nanoscale, familiar rules break down.

buildup.text: Nanomaterials have at least one dimension between 1 and 100 nm — thousands of times smaller than a human hair.

discovery.text: At this scale, surface atoms dominate — a 5 nm particle has 40% of its atoms on the surface versus 0.001% for a marble.

twist.text: Quantum effects kick in too — electrons are confined in such small spaces that energy levels become discrete.

climax.text: Nanomaterials have unique optical, electrical, and chemical properties impossible at larger scales.

punchline.text: Same atoms, wildly different behavior — size changes everything at nanoscale.

quiz.question: Why do nanomaterials behave differently from bulk materials?
options: They are made of different atoms
Surface atoms dominate and quantum confinement alters electronic properties
They are always lighter than bulk materials
